title: In-silico and in-detail experimental interaction studies of new antitumor Zn(II) complex with CT-DNA and serum albumin.
authors: Dorafshan Tabatabai, Ashraf Sadat; Dehghanian, Effat; Mansouri-Torshizi, Hassan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究新型Zn(II)配合物与CT-DNA及血清白蛋白的相互作用，虽涉及DNA结合和分子对接，但对象为小分子金属配合物而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且方法以实验为主、DFT和对接为辅，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: In this study, a novel Zn(II) complex with the formula [Zn(pyrr-ac)(2)] (pyrr-ac: pyrrolidineacetate) was synthesized and characterized through molar conductivity, elemental analysis, (1)H Nuclear Magnetic Resonance ((1)H NMR), UV-Visible spectroscopy, and Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) methods. B3LYP level of DFT method along with aug-cc-pVTZ-PP/6-311G(d,p) basis set was utilized to perform the geometry optimization and HOMO-LUMO analysis. In addition, MEP, NLO and NBO computations were also performed at the same level of theory. In vitro antitumor activity of the mentioned complex on leukemia cell line, K562, was investigated using the MTT assay which surprisingly revealed the effective antitumor activity of the studied zinc complex. Interaction of this compound with biological macromolecules viz., CT-DNA and BSA was studied via different spectroscopic methods. The results of fluorescence experiment displayed that the metal complex binds to both macromolecules through hydrogen bond (H-bond) and van der Waals (vdW) forces. UV-Vis tests indicated a decline in the absorption spectra of CT-DNA/BSA in the presence of the compound. The interaction was further corroborated for CT-DNA via gel electrophoresis, CD spectroscopy and viscosity experiments and for BSA using CD spectroscopy. Furthermore, molecular docking simulation was done to evaluate the nature of interaction between the aforementioned zinc complex and CT-DNA/BSA. These results were in agreement with experimental findings and demonstrated that the main interaction is hydrogen bonding. The above type of investigations may provide a pathway through which zinc complexes join the anticancer category.[Figure: see text]The in-silico and in-vitro results confirm that the newly made [Zn(pyrr-ac)2] complex interacts with CT-DNA than BSA.Communicated by Ramaswamy H. Sarma.
abstract_zh: 在本研究中，合成了一种新型Zn(II)配合物，其化学式为[Zn(pyrr-ac)₂]（pyrr-ac：吡咯烷乙酸酯），并通过摩尔电导率、元素分析、¹H核磁共振（¹H NMR）、紫外-可见光谱和傅里叶变换红外（FT-IR）方法进行了表征。利用DFT方法中的B3LYP级别，结合aug-cc-pVTZ-PP/6-311G(d,p)基组，进行了几何优化和HOMO-LUMO分析。此外，还在相同理论水平上进行了MEP、NLO和NBO计算。通过MTT实验研究了该配合物对白血病细胞系K562的体外抗肿瘤活性，结果令人惊讶地揭示了所研究锌配合物的有效抗肿瘤活性。该化合物与生物大分子（即CT-DNA和BSA）的相互作用通过多种光谱方法进行了研究。荧光实验结果表明，金属配合物通过氢键（H-bond）和范德华力（vdW）与两种大分子结合。UV-Vis测试显示，在化合物存在下，CT-DNA/BSA的吸收光谱出现下降。对于CT-DNA，通过凝胶电泳、CD光谱和粘度实验进一步证实了相互作用；对于BSA，则通过CD光谱进行了验证。此外，进行了分子对接模拟，以评估上述锌配合物与CT-DNA/BSA之间相互作用的性质。这些结果与实验发现一致，表明主要相互作用是氢键。上述类型的研究可能为锌配合物进入抗癌类别提供途径。[图：见正文]计算机模拟和体外实验结果确认，新制备的[Zn(pyrr-ac)₂]配合物与CT-DNA的相互作用强于与BSA的相互作用。由Ramaswamy H. Sarma通讯。
